title: Projects, solutions, packages and analyzers
body: A `.csproj` file is an MSBuild project. SDK-style projects (`<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">`) include every `.cs` file under their folder automatically, so the file mostly holds properties: `TargetFramework` (for example `net10.0`), `OutputType` (`Exe` or a library by default), `Nullable`, `ImplicitUsings`, `LangVersion` and `TreatWarningsAsErrors`. `Directory.Build.props` in a parent folder applies shared properties to every project beneath it.

A solution groups projects. The .NET 10 SDK creates the XML-based `.slnx` format by default (`dotnet new sln`), which is far easier to read and merge than the old `.sln`. `dotnet sln add`, `dotnet add reference` and `dotnet add package` edit these files for you. `global.json` pins the SDK version for a repository and, in .NET 10, selects the test runner.

NuGet packages are referenced with `<PackageReference Include="Name" />`. Central Package Management puts every version in one `Directory.Packages.props` (`ManagePackageVersionsCentrally`), so all projects agree. Commit a lock file (`RestorePackagesWithLockFile`) or at least pin exact versions, and audit dependencies with `dotnet list package --vulnerable`; NuGet audit warnings are on by default.

Analyzers run during compilation. The .NET SDK includes code-quality rules (CA*) and style rules (IDE*); `AnalysisLevel` such as `latest-recommended` chooses how many are enabled, and `.editorconfig` adjusts individual rule severities. Treating warnings as errors in CI keeps nullable and analyzer findings from accumulating.

`dotnet publish -c Release` produces a deployable app. Options include framework-dependent versus self-contained output, a single-file bundle, trimming (`PublishTrimmed`) and Native AOT (`PublishAot`), which compiles ahead of time for fast startup and small memory use but forbids unconstrained reflection and runtime code generation. Check those constraints before choosing AOT.

challenge: Write the contents of a Directory.Packages.props that centrally pins Serilog 4.3.0 and a test project .csproj line that references it without a version, then explain in one sentence why the reference has no Version attribute.
solutionStdout: With central package management the version lives only in Directory.Packages.props, so every project uses the same one.
question: What does Central Package Management change about PackageReference items?
correct: Versions move to Directory.Packages.props and references omit them
wrong: Packages are downloaded once per machine instead of per project
reasoning: One file owns every version, preventing projects in a repository from drifting apart.
